summary: On-demand tool schema fetch loop causing request stalls and intermittent timeouts
description:
Issue summary: HorizonDocs reports a spike in end-to-end latency and a rise in request timeouts for API calls that include function/tool calling. The spike correlates with requests that trigger on-demand schema fetches for external tool integrations. Impact: Around 8% of requests to the customer's production endpoint experienced stalls >5s and ~0.6% timed out (client-facing 499/504) during the incident window. Root cause suspected to be repeated synchronous schema fetches from the function proxy causing extra round-trips and blocking the serving runtime's streaming path.

Impact: Customer-facing latency increase, degraded UX for chat features, and automated retries causing higher token costs. Customer reported some failures appeared to cascade into downstream rate-limit 429s.

Environment: Dedicated pool for HorizonDocs in prod-us-east; Redwood API gateway v2.3.1; function-proxy service v1.9.2; schema-validator v0.8.0 (deployed 2026-03-09).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use HorizonDocs production API key against dedicated endpoint with function-calling enabled and a tool definition not present in local cache
2) Send a streaming chat request that invokes the tool signature (tool name + JSON schema) mid-response
3) Observe server-side logs for repeated GETs to internal schema service and elevated request wall time
4) Re-run with local cache warmed (tool schema pre-fetched) to compare latency delta
logs: 2026-03-10T10:02:15Z [function-proxy] request-id=rdw-9f4a: tool-schema-miss for tool 'horizon.search'; fetching from schema-service
2026-03-10T10:02:17Z [function-proxy] request-id=rdw-9f4a: schema fetch succeeded (200) but validation run blocked streaming for 1400ms
2026-03-10T10:02:17Z [serving-runtime] request-id=rdw-9f4a: streaming stalled waiting for schema validation result
investigation_notes: Support triage: Reproduced locally by creating a request with an uncached tool schema; replication showed an additional 1.2–1.6s of blocking time per uncached tool call.
SRE observation: Schema-service healthy but single-threaded validation loop can block function-proxy worker for the duration of validation when validation is synchronous.
Traffic analysis: Incidents cluster around requests that reference >1 tool per prompt and when requests include nested tool calls (tool A invokes tool B).
Telemetry: Prefix caching reduced mean tail latency by ~40% for affected requests; error rate dropped accordingly.
Related configuration: schema-validator v0.8.0 introduced synchronous strict-validation on first fetch to reduce malformed tool calls (deployed 2026-03-09).
hypothesis: Synchronous schema validation on first fetch created an extra blocking RPC/CPU-bound work on the function-proxy worker, adding ~1–1.5s per uncached tool and preventing streaming tokens from being emitted until validation completes.
Increased wall-time caused clients to hit frontend timeouts and retry, amplifying load and sometimes producing 429s downstream.
Nested or sequential tool calls exacerbate the effect because multiple schema fetchs/validation runs occur within one request path, creating additive blocking.
Dedicated customer's pool had smaller worker concurrency configured (to save costs), making them more sensitive to per-request blocking.
mitigation: Applied immediate workaround (2026-03-10 11:20Z): function-proxy config toggled to use asynchronous schema validation for first fetch (returns cached placeholder and validates in background).
Pre-warmed popular tool schemas for HorizonDocs (bulk cache populate) to avoid on-demand fetches for common tool names.
Increased function-proxy worker concurrency for HorizonDocs' dedicated pool by +2 instances to absorb transient blocking while fix is developed.
Customer advised to enable client-side retry jitter and increase request timeout to reduce perceived failures until patch is available.
resolution_notes: Mitigated: Background validation + cache warm significantly reduced incidents. Engineering is developing a non-blocking validation patch for schema-validator (targeted PR and rollout timeline below). Postmortem and permanent fix planned: make first-fetch validation non-blocking by default with a configurable strictness flag; add metrics to track validation-induced blocking. Customer agreed to rollback strict-validation after test window.
